title: Drawing a line
slide_intent: Teach designers when an illustration can carry an idea that is difficult to photograph. Two shapes can suggest a relationship without requiring a person to stand in for the idea.
strategic_value: Frontline AIDS can give conceptual subjects an energetic visual voice. The familiar heart shape, heavy stroke and vivid color give a reader an immediate point of entry.
demonstration: An oversized illustration pairs two overlapping, oppositely oriented hearts on a cyan field. A separate hand-drawn pink arrow points to the upper edge of one heart.
practical_value: Choose illustration when the message depends on an abstract relationship. Try one large, legible figure before adding supporting details.

content_islands.name: Section rail
content_islands.spec: Run a narrow navigation rail down the left edge. Separate it from the artwork with a vertical rule. Emphasize the Illustration section and retain the book identifier at the foot.

content_islands.name: Purpose statement
content_islands.spec: Place the illustration label, compact uppercase heading and short explanation beside the rail. Give the text a narrow measure and leave room to its right for the main figure.

content_islands.name: Heart illustration
content_islands.spec: Enlarge two heart shapes until the pair occupies most of the page. Outline each with a heavy black stroke, turn one upside down and fill it green. Preserve the cyan background in the other. Use the distinct pink arrow to direct the eye to their contours.
